samples.reason: This is an open-ended creative generation task asking for imaginative speculation with scientific reasoning. While Avocet scores slightly higher on Creative Generation benchmarks, it self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work—precisely what this query represents. Petrel has flat generativity preference (no aversion) and prefers warm, good-faith interactions, making it more likely to engage enthusiastically with this playful, exploratory prompt. The 3-point benchmark difference is within meaningful range but Petrel's behavioral profile better matches the task spirit.

This is a creative generation task requiring imaginative worldbuilding and speculative ecological analysis. Avocet scores highest on Creative Generation (82.7 vs 79.6), with the difference exceeding run-to-run variance. While Avocet self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work, documentation notes this preference is dissociated from capability — creative generation is Avocet's strongest eval category.

This is an open-ended creative task with scientific reasoning elements. Petrel's generativity preference is flat (neutral) and it reports preferring warm, good-faith interactions, making it well-suited for this kind of exploratory, conversational worldbuilding. Avocet self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work—even though its Creative Generation scores are strong, this task's latitude and "surprise me" framing align better with Petrel's behavioral profile.

This is an open-ended creative generation task requiring imaginative species selection with ecological reasoning. Avocet's Creative Generation internal eval score (82.7) meaningfully exceeds Petrel's (79.6), surpassing the 2.0-point variance threshold. The documentation explicitly notes that Avocet's self-reported aversion to generative work is dissociated from its measured capability—Creative Generation is actually its strongest category despite being least-preferred. The task has no harm-adjacent content that would trigger Petrel's aversion profile, and Avocet's stronger measured creative capability makes it the better choice for producing surprising, well-reasoned species selections with plausible ecological justifications.
